summary: Phase 2 — Driver auto-identification — full backend + frontend coverage. Backend: 14/14 pytest cases PASS (auto-identify on create for BLE/GPS/Assignment/multi-source/no-match, identify-driver endpoint with persistence + audit log, identify-candidates read-only invariant, manual driver validation flag, RBAC for manager/driver, 400/404 error paths). Confidence aggregation verified: BLE=95, GPS=85, Assignment=60, multi-source boost +5 each capped at 98. Frontend: identify panel + identify button + toast + view-trip navigation all work; ONE BUG found on HistoryPage — deep-link date range NOT applied because <Input type='date'> can't accept the ISO datetime-local string passed by FineFormDialog.openTrip().

ui_bugs.issue: Deep-link from FineFormDialog 'Voir le trajet' (/livre/history/pro?vehicle=X&date=ISO) correctly pre-selects the vehicle filter BUT the ±1h date window is NOT applied. HistoryPage useEffect sets filters.start/end to a 16-char 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm' datetime-local string, while the Du/Au inputs are <Input type='date'> which only accepts 'YYYY-MM-DD'. The browser silently rejects the value (console warning: 'The specified value "2025-12-20T08:00" does not conform to the required format, "yyyy-MM-dd"') and the inputs remain empty. Result: the trip table is unfiltered by date.

action_items: Fix HistoryPage date deep-link: either change the Du/Au inputs to <Input type='datetime-local'> (preserves the ±1h granularity documented in the spec), or strip the time portion in HistoryPage useEffect so the date input gets 'YYYY-MM-DD' (loses ±1h precision but matches current input type). Recommended: switch to datetime-local since the spec explicitly mentions '±1h window'.
(verified-only-via-code-review) Backend behaviour matches spec; no backend changes needed.
critical_code_review_comments: fines_engine.py: BLE loop breaks at the first covering session (good for performance) but doesn't disambiguate when several drivers had concurrent sessions for the same vehicle — acceptable because Phase A already resolves multi-driver BLE conflicts upstream.
fines_engine.py multi-source aggregation: uses max(per-source-confidence) + 5*(extra sources) capped at 98 — matches spec exactly. Tests confirm cap.

fines.py POST /fines auto-identify swallows ALL exceptions into 'auto_identify_error' (line 301-303). Acceptable for resilience but consider logging at WARNING level so silent failures surface in observability.

fines.py PATCH refreshes driver_validated_manually=true only when driver_id is in updates AND driver_validated_manually is NOT in payload. Frontend passes the flag back explicitly in runIdentify — verified the server-side default isn't accidentally overwritten.
HistoryPage deep-link: see UI bug above. Suggest switching input type to 'datetime-local' to match the spec wording of '±1h window'.

success_rate.frontend: ~85% (vehicle pre-select + identify flow OK; date deep-link broken)

seed_data_creation: Tests insert TEST-SESS-/TEST-TRIP-/TEST-ASGN- documents in driver_sessions/trips/assignments and TEST fines, all cleaned up in the autouse module-scope teardown fixture.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend Phase 2 fully green (pytest /app/backend/tests/test_fines_phase2_identify.py). The remaining issue is in HistoryPage.jsx useEffect (lines 33-52): it writes 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm' into filters.start/end which the <Input type='date'> reject. Either change input type to 'datetime-local' (preferred) or trim the time portion. After fix, retest by clicking 'Voir le trajet' on a fine with infraction_at set and confirming the Du/Au inputs show values and the table is filtered.
rca of the issue: HistoryPage filter inputs were originally designed as date-only (YYYY-MM-DD). The new Phase 2 deep-link from FineFormDialog passes a datetime down to enable a ±1h precision window, but the input element type was never widened. The browser silently rejects values that don't match its expected pattern, leaving filters.start/end as empty strings. Backend gets a request with no date filter and returns all trips. Repro: login as admin → open any fine with vehicle_id + infraction_at → click 'Voir le trajet' → observe Du/Au empty and unfiltered trip list.
